summary: Hiromichi Kato is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Ryogon Fukuhara as a graduate student. He taught Collett Cox and held a post as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Hiromitsu Ikuma works in Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate at Tohoku University by 2019 and held researcher posts at the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies and Taisho University (attested 2020).
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and served there as a professor from circa 1970 to 1990.
Hironari Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued PhD studies (attested 2015–2020) and held a post at Bukkyo University. He was also a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hironobu Minami works in Buddhist studies. He was a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He taught Waso Harada and was a professor at Mie Chukyo University (attested 1982).

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1981). He held posts at Morioka College (~1989–1993) and Tohoku University (~2001–2019 as professor).

Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University (~1980–1986) and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1988–1998), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (~1998).

Hiroshi Araki is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees and a PhD at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held lecturer positions at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Hokkaido University.
Hiroshi Kanaseki was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1948–1952) and held a post at Tenri University from circa 1960 to 1997.

Hiroshi Kanno is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1984). He served as director at Soka University and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2009), succeeding Yuichi Kajiyama.

Hiroshi Kuroda specializes in Indology and philosophy, having completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University by 1976. He served as an associate professor at Osaka Gakuin University (~1982–1991) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (~1984–1990).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied under Albrecht Wezler. He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Osaka University and head of the Ayurveda Research Society (both attested 1987).
Hiroshi Nemoto works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he also served as a professor (attested 2015–2016 and 2026).
Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and special appointment lecturer (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied abroad at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
